answer:
**Three useful replies should offer distinct plausible intentions, not three paraphrases of one answer.** For an invitation, “Yes,” “Sounds good,” and “Absolutely” provide little choice. Acceptance, a relevant clarification, and a polite decline may cover different needs when the email supports them. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084) [2](https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/)

Generate or retrieve a broader pool, score relevance and appropriateness, then penalize similarity to already selected replies. MMR provides one way to trade relevance against redundancy. Intent clustering can prevent wording differences from being mistaken for meaningful diversity.

**Diversity cannot override context.** Do not invent commitments, availability, or personal facts merely to fill three slots. If only one safe useful intent is supported, forcing contradictory alternatives can make the product worse.

Evaluate selections, edits before sending, and semantic coverage. A frequently selected suggestion may still require substantial correction, so selection rate alone is insufficient. Suggestions should remain drafts until the user chooses to send. The model's job is to reduce composition effort while preserving the user's control over meaning and action.

**Technical details and references.**

Generate or retrieve a larger pool, score relevance to the email, then cluster or rerank for distinct **intent**, not merely different wording. MMR can penalize semantic similarity to already selected replies while retaining relevance. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084) [2](https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/)

For example, offer acceptance, a clarifying question, and a polite decline when context supports all three, rather than three synonyms of agreement. Do not force diversity by proposing an inappropriate or contradictory answer. Exclude unsupported commitments, sensitive content, and replies requiring information the user has not provided. Evaluate selection rate, edit burden, semantic coverage, and accidental-send risk. Suggestions remain drafts until the user chooses to send.
